instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 inch baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Dice the bell pepper and the onion, mince the garlic and chop the parsley.
Cook the spaghetti in the boiling water until just al dente, following the package time. Drain it.

Meanwhile, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef, the bell pepper, the onion, the garlic and the salt. Break the beef up as it cooks and cook for about 8 minutes, until the beef is browned and no pink is left. Spoon off any extra fat.
Stir in the pasta sauce, the diced tomatoes with their juices and the Italian seasoning. Simmer, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes, until thickened.
Stir the drained spaghetti and the parsley into the sauce.
Transfer it to the baking dish. Scatter the mozzarella and the Parmesan over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until it's hot and the cheese is browned and bubbling.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Cut it into squares to serve.
Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat a square in the microwave until hot all the way through.
method_notes: Spend With Pennies is the lead (4.98 from 513): beef, pepper and onion cooked in a skillet, simmered in jarred sauce and diced tomatoes, tossed with the spaghetti, topped with mozzarella and Parmesan and baked at 375°F. The source is a 16 oz pound of spaghetti for 8; this is cut to 12 oz of spaghetti with the sauce scaled to match, so it still makes a full pan with leftovers. Other versions mix in an egg and milk or layer a cottage cheese filling; this one keeps to the lead.
